title: Loop instance configuration
description: EPIC-030 T930. The programme-defined half of a governed workflow type (FR-GEL-004, FR-GEL-005, FR-GEL-009). The tenant-configured half — authorities, gates, trigger rules — lives in the loop_instance_configurations row keyed to this file. `stages` is programme-defined and NOT writable by a tenant. The executable conformance check is backend/tests/architecture/loop-config-conformance.spec.ts; this schema documents the shape, that check enforces it, and the check is the authority where the two could disagree.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped when this shape changes. A file with no version is a file nobody can migrate.

workflowType.description: Unique per programme; the file is named <workflowType>.json. FR-GEL-004 — each type resolves its own configuration, so two Rooms cannot share one and collapse into a single governed surface (ADR-0018).

stages.description: A subset of LOOP_STAGES, in model order (FR-GEL-009). Omitted stages are LEGAL and VISIBLE: FR-GEL-008 requires them to appear in the progress projection as omitted, not as absent, so 'configured not to apply' and 'not reached' stay distinguishable.

from.description: Must be one of this file's stages.

to.description: Must be one of this file's stages.

requiredGates.description: FR-GEL-020 — a transition carries its named required gates. Empty is legal and explicit; absent is not, because 'no gates' and 'nobody said' must not look alike.

trigger.description: null for a human transition, or a named rule for an automated one. FR-GEL-031 and RULE-11: a trigger that exists without naming its rule is the invisible automation the rule forbids, which is why 'present but anonymous' is not expressible here.

approvedBy.description: FR-GEL-016 — the actor identity that approved this configuration. Absent and the configuration does not load; a governed workflow nobody authorised is not governed.

approvalRef.description: The reviewed commit under R-030-7's interim gate; the EPIC-031 decision id once that Epic lands. Both spellings satisfy the same requirement, which is why the field is a string rather than a typed reference.
